children: Vail Resorts logged a wider loss and near-flat revenue in the fiscal fourth quarter, as it wrapped up a year hounded by unfavorable skiing weather.
The ski resort company on Monday posted a loss attributable to Vail of $190.2 million, or $5.34 a share, compared with a loss of $182.4 million, or $4.99 a share, a year earlier.
Revenue rose 0.3% to $278.1 million. Analysts surveyed by FactSet forecast revenue of $269.3 million.
Conditions in Australia were unfavorable during the quarter, Vail said. Cumulative snowfall in the region was about 57% below the 10-year average, which pressured visitation and revenue.
Pass product unit sales through Sept. 18 for the upcoming 2026-27 North American ski season decreased about 12%. Days sold and sales dollars also decreased compared with the same time last year.

"This past winter was one of the most challenging winters in history across the western U.S. for the ski industry, which negatively impacted financial performance for the year," Chief Executive Rob Katz said.
Conditions were especially severe in the Rockies, where snowfall and snowpack was near historic lows, he said.
In the new fiscal year, Vail expects net income attributable to the company to be $158 million to $233 million. Analysts are projecting $207.4 million, according to FactSet.

The guidance reflects Vail's accelerated realization of $5 million from the next phase of its turnaround plan. The company also expects $25 million in savings during fiscal year 2028 that includes a portion of capital savings.
